meanings.en: to become hungry, work up an appetite
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'голодаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got hungry', paired with 'голодать'.

examples.trans: Good evening, a bottle of red wine, the best in our cellar.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wine collection / cellar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, бутылочка красного вина, лучшая в нашей винотеке.
examples.trans: Good evening, a bottle of red wine, the best in our cellar.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть винотека.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always wine collection.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pregnant women' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А беременным разве можно вино?
examples.trans: Are pregnant women really allowed wine?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть беременная.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always pregnant women.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'really, can it be', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну мы же разобрались, ну ошибся.
examples.trans: Well we already sorted it out, I made a mistake.

examples.text: В следующий раз играйте с директором завода.
examples.trans: Next time play with a factory director.

examples.text: Почему ты сразу не сказал: не было, нет и не будет?
examples.trans: Why did you not say right away: there was not, is not, and will not be?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Рядом с женщиной должен быть мужчина, на которого можно опереться.
examples.trans: Next to a woman there should be a man she can lean on.

examples.text: Кто съест антрекот, может за него не платить.
examples.trans: Whoever eats the entrecote does not have to pay for it.

examples.text: Вы выиграли возможность прокатиться с обаятельным поваром.
examples.trans: You have won the chance to go for a ride with a charming cook.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: А это что такое? Тоже сюрприз для Феди?
examples.trans: And what is this? Also a surprise for Fedya?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('expensive').

examples.text: Такое дорогое можно, бутылочка на шестерых.
examples.trans: Such expensive wine is allowed, one bottle for six people.

examples.text: Дорогой, спасибо тебе за твою щедрость.
examples.trans: Darling, thank you for your generosity.

examples.text: Это дорогая одежда.
examples.trans: These are expensive clothes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не называй меня олигархом.
examples.trans: Do not call me an oligarch.

examples.text: А как же мне тебя называть?
examples.trans: Then what should I call you?

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'six people', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Такое дорогое можно, бутылочка на шестерых.
examples.trans: Such expensive wine is allowed, one bottle for six people.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно шестеро и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite six people and calmly.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'generosity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Дорогой, спасибо тебе за твою щедрость.
examples.trans: Darling, thank you for your generosity.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть щедрость.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always generosity.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hope', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вы меня поняли.
examples.trans: I hope you understood me.

examples.text: Я надеюсь. Идите, действуйте быстрее!
examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

examples.text: Я надеюсь.
examples.trans: I hope so.

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'is liked, pleases', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.

examples.text: Тебе понравился фильм?
examples.trans: Did you like the film?

examples.text: Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.
